rule: good. stored as a relation between the two kinds, which is the right reading for a claim about mist-light and nightmoths in general rather than about any one moth.
texts: good. fires once per showing, with the lantern, the night, the mist-light and the moths all covered and the attracting tied to its trigger.
good. the same fireable per-occurrence shape as the "when" version, with the drawing tied back to the showing.
good. the denial distributes to each nightmoth as a rule at strength 0, and "ordinary firelight" keeps both of its parts (firelight, and ordinary).

mixed: the rule fires at the right "rarely" strength, but "on cold nights" is swept inside what is rare, so the existence of a cold night and its coldness are themselves asserted only at rarely-strength instead of picking out the occasions being quantified. Rewrite as "When a night is cold, nightmoths rarely fly." so the coldness becomes the condition and the rarity applies to the flying alone.
